meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Rapamycin is not an ordinary inhibitor: it first binds the small protein FKBP12, and only the two-part complex is the real drug.
data.mechanism_beginner: Rapamycin doesn't work alone – it first has to team up with a helper protein called FKBP12.
data.boundary: X-ray crystallography and in vitro work on bovine, rat and mouse material (CHO1996, BRO1994, SAB1995). Describes drug binding in purified systems; it says nothing about dose or effect in patients.
data.note: The molecular-glue concept - genuinely surprising to newcomers.
